title: Bunya Pine: Great Bunya Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The heaviest cone of any conifer, up to ten kilograms, falls from as much as 28 metres up. Three bunya pines mapped, in Porto, Bucaco and Barcelona.
intro: The bunya pine drops the heaviest cone of any conifer on earth: up to ten kilograms, roughly a bowling ball, from a crown that can be twenty-eight metres up. In southeast Queensland, the only place it grows wild, the trees fruit heavily every few years, and Aboriginal groups travelled hundreds of kilometres for the gatherings that followed. Australian parks now sign and fence them for the obvious reason. Europe planted them for the silhouette instead: a straight column with branches in flat symmetrical whorls and leaves stiff enough to draw blood. Porto's is the tallest thing in the Jardim da Cordoaria at roughly 40 metres. Bucaco's is five metres round beside a hotel that was still a Carmelite convent when it was planted. Barcelona's has been in the Teatre Grec gardens since about 1920.
